findings.title: Firewall permits world-sourced administrative traffic
findings.rationale: The ingress allow rule includes SSH or RDP ports from a world CIDR. This does not establish the presence or reachability of a target VM.
findings.remediation: Restrict source ranges and target scope; use IAP or an approved private access path.

findings.title: Proposed project-level basic role grant
findings.rationale: Owner and editor grant broad project permissions. This is a least-privilege review, not evidence of internet exposure.
findings.remediation: Replace basic roles with narrowly scoped predefined or reviewed custom roles.

findings.title: Planned deletion of a persistent resource
findings.rationale: Deletion or replacement can disrupt service or remove data; backup state and recovery readiness are not established by this plan.
findings.remediation: Require human review of ownership, dependencies, backups and a tested recovery plan.

findings.title: Proposed public Cloud Storage object-read grant
findings.rationale: Public principals receive object-read permissions; exposure depends on prevention policies and any IAM conditions.
findings.remediation: Remove public principals; use scoped identities and enforce public access prevention.

explanation: The deterministic Terraform review identified four findings involving administrative firewall rules, project permissions, data destruction, and public access grants that require operator attention prior to deployment.

advisory.summary: The deterministic Terraform review identified four findings involving administrative firewall rules, project permissions, data destruction, and public access grants that require operator attention prior to deployment.

explanations.text: The proposed configuration allows SSH administrative traffic (port 22) from any IP address (0.0.0.0/0). This represents an administrative ingress path, although the actual presence or reachability of a target VM cannot be established from the plan alone.
The proposed grant assigns a basic project role (roles/owner) which expands administrative capabilities. This represents an authorization risk rather than direct proof of internet exposure.

The plan requests the deletion of a persistent Cloud Storage bucket. A destructive action presents a service disruption or data loss risk; backup readiness and recovery capabilities are not verified by this plan.

The plan proposes granting object-read access (roles/storage.objectViewer) to allUsers. This public principal grant conflicts with private access goals, though effective exposure depends on bucket-level and organizational prevention policies.

recommendations: Restrict firewall ingress rules to validated, scoped private networks or use an access proxy such as IAP.
Replace broad project roles with narrowly scoped, predefined or custom IAM roles mapped to operational needs.
Verify database and bucket backup retention, integrity, and restore procedures locally before applying deletions.
Remove allUsers from object-read permissions and configure public access prevention on the bucket.
limitations: The plan facts do not establish if a VM exists, listens on the target port, or has a public IP assigned.
Sanitized payloads omit IAM conditions and parent organization policies, leaving effective permission states uncertain.
The proposed actions do not verify whether backup copies exist, are valid, or have been successfully tested.
A model explanation is supporting guidance and does not constitute authorization to modify or apply infrastructure.
